sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN PLAINS AREA THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: THE MAIN BELT OF WESTERLIES WILL REMAIN ACROSS THE NRN TIER OF STATES...WITH THE PRIMARY EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGH PROGRESSING EWD/SEWD OVER ONTARIO. FARTHER S...A SERIES OF LOW-AMPLITUDE SPEED MAXIMA WILL MOVE NEWD FROM NV/UT TO WY...NEB/SD...AND THEN SEWD TO THE MID MS VALLEY. ONE PROMINENT WAVE IN THIS SEQUENCE HAS BEEN ENHANCED BY OVERNIGHT CONVECTION OVER SD/MN...AND IT WILL MOVE ESEWD ACROSS IA THIS AFTERNOON NE MO/IL OVERNIGHT. THE INITIAL MORNING CONVECTION OVER NW IA/SW MN WILL LIKELY WEAKEN LATER THIS MORNING AS THE STORMS ENCOUNTER A MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT WITHIN A WEAK SURFACE RIDGE ACROSS IL/IA. HOWEVER...THERE WILL BE SOME POTENTIAL FOR ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT LATER THIS AFTERNOON AS RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE SPREADS NEWD IN ADVANCE OF THE MCV AND REMNANT CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS...IN ADVANCE OF THE SURFACE COLD FRONT WHICH WILL LIKEWISE MOVE SEWD INTO NEB/IA. A WEAKENING CAP WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES FROM 1500-3000 J/KG ARE EXPECTED IN THE WARM SECTOR...ALONG WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 35-45 KT. THIS COMBINATION OF INGREDIENTS WILL FAVOR SUPERCELLS INITIALLY WITH THE POTENTIAL TO PRODUCE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. CONVECTION MAY ALSO GROW UPSCALE INTO ONE OR MORE

sections.title: AZ THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: ELY MIDLEVEL FLOW AND MOIST PROFILES ARE PREVALENT OVER CENTRAL/SRN AZ AGAIN THIS MORNING. WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT AN EMBEDDED SPEED MAX WILL MOVE WWD TODAY FROM SW NM TO SRN AZ TODAY...THOUGH IT MAY PASS THE HIGHER TERRAIN IN SE AZ PRIOR TO PEAK HEATING. THUS...THE ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT SOME DOWNBURST POTENTIAL WITH STORMS MOVING WWD INTO THE LOWER DESERTS...BUT STORM COVERAGE/INTENSITY ARE SOMEWHAT IN QUESTION. FOR THESE REASONS...WILL MAINTAIN LOW DAMAGING WIND PROBABILITIES...BUT AZ NEAR AND S OF THE RIM WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED THROUGH THE DAY FOR EVIDENCE OF STRONGER INSTABILITY AND GREATER STORM COVERAGE THAN CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY TO THE SE ATLANTIC COAST THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: AS WITH PREVIOUS DAYS...A RELATIVELY BROAD AREA WILL HAVE THE POTENTIAL FOR AFTERNOON DOWNBURSTS WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED WIND DAMAGE. CONVECTION WILL DEVELOP WITH DAYTIME HEATING TO THE S OF A WEAKENING COLD FRONT ACROSS MO/KY...AND ALONG RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM CONVECTION LATE YESTERDAY. SOME WEAK LARGE SCALE SUPPORT FOR CONVECTION WILL COME IN THE FORM OF A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH AXIS /WITH EMBEDDED VORTICITY MAXIMA/ FROM AR TO NC. HOWEVER...THE WIDESPREAD CONVECTION ALSO APPEARS TO HAVE REDUCED INSTABILITY SINCE YESTERDAY...SO STORM INTENSITY COULD BE SOMEWHAT REDUCED COMPARED TO MONDAY. ..THOMPSON/LEITMAN.. 07/05/2011

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: MORNING SATELLITE AND RADAR LOOPS SHOW AREAS OF REMNANT CONVECTION OVER PARTS OF NORTHERN NEB AND WESTERN IA. A SURFACE BOUNDARY IS SAGGING SOUTHWARD FROM THIS AREA AND EXTENDS ACROSS CENTRAL NEB. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT THE STRONGEST DAYTIME HEATING AND DESTABILIZATION WILL OCCUR SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY AND AWAY FROM THE CURRENT CONVECTION...MAINLY OVER SOUTHERN NEB AND NORTHERN KS. IT APPEARS LIKELY THAT A CORRIDOR OF STRONG CAPE VALUES WILL DEVELOP BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON IN THIS REGION...ALONG WITH A RATHER WEAK CAP. SCATTERED AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP OVER SOUTHERN NEB AND SPREAD EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD TOWARD NORTHWEST MO AFTER DARK. SUFFICIENT EFFECTIVE SHEAR WILL PROMOTE ORGANIZED MULTICELL OR SUPERCELL STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: ERN CO/WY/MT
sections.text: MOST MODEL SOLUTIONS SHOW A LIKELIHOOD OF SCATTERED CONVECTION LATER TODAY OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF CENTRAL CO/WY AND SOUTHEAST MT. THESE STORMS WILL SPREAD INTO THE ADJACENT PLAINS DURING THE LATE AFTERNOON AND EVENING. STEEP LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR SUGGEST A RISK OF A FEW HIGH-BASED SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL.

sections.title: AZ
sections.text: THERE HAVE BEEN ONLY SUBTLE CHANGES TO THE OVERALL PATTERN ACROSS AZ DURING THE PAST 2-3 DAYS. RATHER HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT ACROSS THE AREA WILL ONCE AGAIN RESULT IN MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY OVER CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN AZ. WATER VAPOR LOOPS SHOWS A WEAK MID LEVEL FEATURE MOVING FROM WESTERN NM INTO AZ. STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND AN EASTERLY COMPONENT TO THE STEERING FLOW WILL HELP ANY CONVECTION THAT FORMS OVER EASTERN AZ TO SPREAD INTO THE LOWER DESERTS. WHILE THOSE STORMS THAT FORM WILL POSE A LOCALIZED THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS...IT IS ONCE AGAIN UNCERTAIN IF STORMS WILL BE ABLE TO GAIN SUFFICIENT MASS TO PRODUCE A LARGER COLD POOL...WHICH WOULD POSE A MORE WIDESPREAD RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS. WILL MAINTAIN ONLY LOW SEVERE PROBS AT THIS TIME DUE TO THESE UNCERTAINTIES.

sections.title: AL/GA/CAROLINAS
sections.text: ANOTHER DAY OF SCATTERED AFTERNOON SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS IS ANTICIPATED OVER THE SOUTHEAST STATES FROM AL INTO THE CAROLINAS. NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS YESTERDAY HAVE LESSENED THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY AND MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES TODAY...WHICH SHOULD GENERALLY DECREASE THE INTENSITY OF THE DOWNDRAFTS/WIND THREAT. NEVERTHELESS...GUSTY TO DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE IN THE STRONGER CORES TODAY ACROSS THE REGION. ..HART/ROGERS.. 07/05/2011

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS SEWD INTO THE MID MO VALLEY
sections.text: ISOLATED STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED FROM THE HIGH PLAINS OF ERN MT SWD INTO NERN CO...WHERE HEATING/DESTABILIZATION HAS COMBINED WITH UPSLOPE FLOW. WITH MID-LEVEL RIDGING LIKELY TO CONTINUE LIMITING CONVECTIVE COVERAGE -- PARTICULARLY ACROSS ERN MT...THREAT SHOULD REMAIN FAIRLY ISOLATED. GREATER CONCENTRATION OF STORMS/SEVERE POTENTIAL APPEARS TO EXIST FROM NERN CO EWD...WITH A CLUSTER OF STORMS MOVING EWD ACROSS NERN CO AND A SECOND SHIFTING SWD ACROSS SERN NEB INTO NRN KS. WITH ESELY LOW-LEVEL JET PROGGED TO INCREASE INTO NWRN KS OVERNIGHT AND AN AXIS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY EXTENDING E NEAR AND JUST N OF THE KS BORDER...CONVECTION SHOULD CONTINUE TO ROLL EWD/ESEWD WITH ASSOCIATED THREATS FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. FARTHER E...THE AFOREMENTIONED INSTABILITY AXIS TURNS SEWD ACROSS ROUGHLY THE ERN HALF OF KS. HERE...THE FAIRLY ORGANIZED SWD-MOVING STORM CLUSTER WILL CONTINUE TO BE FUELED BY SAID INSTABILITY -- AGAIN POSING A MORE CONCENTRATED SEVERE THREAT THROUGH THIS EVENING.

sections.title: DESERT SW
sections.text: DIURNALLY-DRIVEN STORMS CONTINUE ACROSS THE DESERT SW...WHERE HEATING HAS YIELDED MODERATE INSTABILITY -- MAINLY FROM THE LOWER ELEVATIONS OF AZ WWD INTO PARTS OF SRN CA. ISOLATED WIND GUSTS AND SOME HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY STRONGER STORM. SOMEWHAT GREATER SEVERE POTENTIAL EXISTS ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL AND SRN AZ...WHERE MID-LEVEL ELYS WILL CONTINUE SUPPORTING WWD PROGRESSION OF MORE ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS -- WHICH HAVE EVOLVED IN PART DUE TO GREATER INSTABILITY IN THIS REGION. GIVEN THE MORE ORGANIZED CONVECTION AND THUS GREATER POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WINDS...WILL MAINTAIN SLIGHT RISK ACROSS THIS AREA.

sections.title: THE SOUTHEAST
sections.text: LARGE AREA OF CONVECTION CONTINUES ACROSS THE MID SOUTH/SOUTHEAST AND WWD TO THE ARKLATEX/E TX THIS EVENING...WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MODERATE INSTABILITY AND WEAK FLOW ALOFT. ISOLATED THREATS FOR HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS WILL CONTINUE WITH STRONGER CELLS...THOUGH AN OVERALL DECREASE IN SEVERE THREAT -- AND STORMS IN GENERAL -- CAN BE EXPECTED THROUGH THE EVENING. ..GOSS.. 07/06/2011
